report.summary: Chunk 4 of 5: builds document links, type edges, temporal edges, and hyperedges from index data, with deduplication and validation.
risks: line 361-395 | medium | Document link layer: uses sorted() on dict items; order deterministic but may be costly for large dicts. | Profile with realistic index size.

line 397-440 | medium | Type edges: deduplication key includes attributes; function consuming same type via different params kept separate. | Verify with test case of duplicate edges with different attributes.
line 442-463 | medium | Temporal edges: uses sorted((a,b)) to canonicalize undirected pair; may lose directionality. | Confirm intended semantics for co_change edges.
line 465-475 | medium | Hyperedge construction starts but incomplete in chunk; may lead to incomplete forest if chunk ends abruptly. | Check next chunk for completion.
todos: Verify that document link source/target validation (source not in module_ids) is correct for links to external documents.
Confirm that type edge source may be a file (for consumes/produces) and attributes carry function_ref.
Check that temporal edge lift defaults to 1.0 when missing or zero.
Review hyperedge construction in next chunk.

claims.text: A link says "this document refers to that file"; an import says "this code cannot run without that file". Merging them would silently move ``fan_in`` and every reachability answer derived from the import layer, including the safety fence's dominance fraction.
claims.why: The claim about fan_in, reachability, and dominance fraction refers to behavior elsewhere in the forest. This chunk only builds edges; it does not compute those metrics.

claims.text: Absent key -> empty loop -> byte-identical forest, so an index built without documents produces the forest it always produced.
claims.why: The code uses index.get('document_links') or {}, which yields empty dict if key missing, leading to zero iterations.

claims.text: The endpoint gate is asymmetric and that is not an oversight: a TARGET is always a type-kind node, while a SOURCE may also be a file, because ``consumes``/``produces`` start at a FUNCTION and functions are not forest nodes -- so those two attach to the file that declares the function and carry its identity in ``attributes["function_ref"]``.
claims.why: Code checks: target must be in type_ids; source may be in module_ids or type_ids. Attributes are preserved from row. The claim about function_ref is uncheckable because it refers to the content of attributes, which is not validated here.

claims.text: Deduplicated on the FULL row, not on the pair: one function can legitimately consume the same type twice through two different parameters, and collapsing those two would delete the ``param`` evidence that makes the edge worth publishing.
claims.why: Deduplication key includes canonicalized attributes, so edges with same source/target/relation but different attributes are kept separate.

claims.text: Two byte-identical rows, on the other hand, are one fact stated twice.
claims.why: If two rows have identical relation, source, target, and attributes, the key will match and the second will be skipped.

claims.text: Anything else is dropped in silence rather than manufactured: an edge to a type node the index did not publish is missing evidence, and inventing the endpoint would make the forest disagree with the index it was normalised from.
claims.why: If target not in type_ids, continue; if source not in either set, continue. No edge is created, no error raised.

observations.what: Document link edges are added with relation 'documents' and directed=True.
Type edges use relation name from index; reserved relations are skipped via _RESERVED_RELATIONS.
Temporal edges use sorted pair to canonicalize undirected edges.
Lift value defaults to 1.0 if missing or zero (max(0.0, float(...) or 0.0)).
Hyperedge construction begins but chunk ends before completion; cluster iteration and member processing is incomplete.
